title: IDOR and broken access control runner: detect insecure direct object references and horizontal/vertical privilege escalation
goal: WebGoat has dedicated idor and missingac modules. IDOR is OWASP A01:2021 (Broken Access Control — the #1 category). AegisPT's biz-logic-probe is very limited. Implement a dedicated idor-bac runner: (1) Object ID enumeration: for endpoints with numeric/sequential IDs in paths (/api/users/123, /orders/456, /files/789), substitute the authenticated user's ID with adjacent IDs (123±1, ±5, ±10, random) and check if responses differ (access denied vs data returned). Finding: 'IDOR - Horizontal Privilege Escalation'. (2) Role parameter manipulation: identify endpoints with role or admin parameters in request body/query. Change role=user to role=admin, isAdmin=false to isAdmin=true. Finding: 'Broken Access Control - Privilege Escalation via Parameter'. (3) Method override: test if DELETE/PUT/PATCH is accessible when only GET is shown in UI (X-HTTP-Method-Override header bypass). (4) Path-based bypass: try /admin, /dashboard/admin, /.env, /api/admin/users without authentication. (5) UUID replacement: for UUID-based IDs, test with known UUIDs from previous responses (user A accessing user B's data). All tests use credentials from configured accounts. Active tier — requires authenticated access. Produces Critical/High findings for confirmed IDOR.
scope: Gap analysis 2026-05-03: WebGoat idor and missingac modules. OWASP A01:2021 (Broken Access Control) is the #1 web vulnerability. AegisPT's biz-logic-probe runner exists but barely covers this. Burp Suite Pro + Autorize extension detects IDOR automatically by replaying requests with different session tokens.
generation_reason: OWASP #1 vulnerability (Broken Access Control/IDOR) is poorly covered — WebGoat has dedicated modules, Burp has Autorize extension, AegisPT has minimal coverage.
